profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (QTS Ashburn-Shellhorn / ASH3 campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, this Ashburn-Shellhorn DC1 (ASH3 DC1) facility sits at 22291 Shellhorn Rd, Ashburn, VA 20147, part of a 25-acre, two-building campus with 80+ MW critical campus capacity; per-building sqft/MW allocation is not published.

QTS Data Centers (shown on this row under its pre-2013-IPO name, "Quality Technology Services") was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas. Per Blackstone's own press release, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT) and other Blackstone-affiliated funds completed a roughly $10 billion acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021, taking the company private at $78 per share; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. QTS's own site lists its US headquarters at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, Virginia, placing this Northern Virginia "Data Center Alley" corridor, alongside neighboring hyperscale and colocation campuses from Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, at the center of the company's operations.

Dominion Energy, the dominant electric utility across Northern Virginia's data center corridor, has repeatedly cited data center demand growth as a primary driver of its long-term transmission and generation planning, and Loudoun and Prince William County officials have both cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a significant share of their county budgets. QTS's Virginia campuses sit within this same regional grid and policy environment as neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, all tracked elsewhere in this registry.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model shared with peers like Digital Realty and CyrusOne in this same Northern Virginia corridor; under Blackstone ownership since 2021, QTS has continued expanding its US footprint (including its Manassas and Richmond 3 campuses, both still under construction as of the facts recorded here) rather than slowing development after going private.

profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Northern Virginia campus, spanning Loudoun County (Ashburn-Shellhorn, Ashburn-Moran, Ashburn Lockridge buildings), Prince William County (Manassas DC1, DC2, DC5), and Sterling (Ashburn 1, Ashburn 2). Northern Virginia is confirmed by Wikipedia as one of QTS's primary operating regions, alongside the separate Richmond, VA campus recorded elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
The Ashburn-Shellhorn DC1 facility sits on a 25-acre Northern Virginia campus operated by QTS, a Blackstone-owned data center operator founded in 2003. The campus spans two buildings with a combined critical capacity of 80 MW or greater, though QTS does not publish the megawatt allocation between them. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 80 MW of IT load suggests roughly 2,000 racks as a campus total, assuming standard power delivery efficiency.

This facility is part of QTS's larger Northern Virginia footprint, which includes additional buildings in Loudoun and Prince William counties. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 operators publish power capacity figures, totaling 1,375 MW. At 80 MW or above, this campus ranks 24th in published Virginia capacity, placing it in the upper quartile of disclosed facilities statewide but below the state's largest single operators.

The campus qualifications and tenant list are not published. The facility's relevance to AI scaling depends on whether its capacity serves the training, inference, or research workloads driving current demand, information not disclosed in the operator's public specifications.
